design: neutral timestamped synchronous interface contract review
skill_title: Derive event phases before an executable timing challenge
pattern: A timestamped table is silently treated as either pre-edge input values or post-edge drives, so an executable challenge shifts acceptance and completion by one cycle while appearing precise.
when: Reviewing a generated reference model, waveform replay or proposed executable challenge whose visible prose and timing rows must jointly define synchronous behavior.
what: Keep Program First: run `professional_tb_gen.py` through the normal producer and freeze its exact output and raw evidence. An independent IC expert then derives from the whole visible contract the input drive phase, capture edge, settled sample point, output-valid interval, transaction overlap, reset behavior and any condition-specific don't-care. Cite the source for each decision and distinguish requirements from assumptions. Where a timestamp admits pre-edge values and post-edge drives, explain both schedules and their observable consequences; choose the best source-bound interpretation using all visible prose, diagrams and tables before declaring ambiguity. Neither a table timestamp alone nor simulator scheduling, a DUT trace, prior score or hidden oracle supplies normative authority. Encode the chosen phase explicitly in the challenge, avoiding a drive/sample race and observing settled outputs. A disagreement still needs a prompt-derived executable proof that fails the frozen Program output; repair must pass the same unchanged challenge, normal gates and a fresh independent review. Do not apply a universal one-cycle correction or grant automatic PASS. If independent adjudication leaves two interpretations equally supported, preserve both and report the affected timing claim `NOT_MEASURED` with the exact missing convention; keep separately determined checks in scope. This review guidance prevents an error and does not itself prove a functional recovery.
example: A neutral contract has a 10 ns clock, a request row at a rising timestamp of 40 ns, and completion two full periods after request acceptance. If the row describes the value present before the edge, acceptance is at 40 ns and completion at 60 ns. If it describes a drive after the edge, acceptance is at 50 ns and completion at 70 ns. Visible prose saying the request is stable before the listed edge selects the first schedule; a table without that statement requires the rest of the contract to adjudicate. Define the settled observation point and valid interval in either schedule instead of shifting every expectation by one cycle.
generality: Timestamped synchronous specifications occur in controllers, pipelines and streaming interfaces. The reasoning concerns event semantics and source authority, not any design identifier or stored solution. Existing generators and execution consumers retain their proof responsibilities.
why_not_bucket_a: The exact input is visible prose, diagrams and timestamped signal rows that may omit whether a row is a pre-edge value or a post-edge drive; no closed regex or structural rule can select the normative phase for all such contracts, so whole-contract engineering adjudication is required while existing programs still generate and execute the chosen test.
before_state: The supplied completed-review handoff identifies an executable challenge that silently selected a table phase and could move completion by one cycle; this packet does not independently replay that case.
after_state: The general testbench judgment skill now requires explicit whole-contract phase derivation, source-bound alternative adjudication and honest unresolved scope before using a timing challenge.
ai_reasoning: An executable assertion proves only its encoded temporal interpretation. Making the test runnable does not establish that the interpretation follows from the visible contract. The missing operation is independent engineering review of the normative event phases, not a deterministic one-cycle correction.
capture_scope: Review-error prevention only; no recovered design, fresh blind score, native execution or acceptance claim.
